newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arabs may use normalisation card to punish Israel.
newsitem.headline: Arabs may use normalisation card to punish Israel.

text.p: Arab foreign ministers gathered in Cairo on Sunday to coordinate a campaign to punish Israel for its settlement policies in Jerusalem, and many said that freezing ties with the Jewish state would be a fitting penalty.
At recent meetings in Islamabad and Rabat, Arab officials have said they would reconsider relations with Israel unless it stopped building a Jewish settlement in disputed East Jerusalem.
Some of the officials, in Cairo for a regular meeting of the 22-member Arab League, proposed cutting ties with Israel altogether.
"Ceasing normalisation with Israel is a way to pressure it, as was decided in the Rabat and Islamabad meetings," Algerian Foreign Minister Ahmed Attaf told reporters in Cairo.
"The Arab League must follow suit and take a position that is both clear and strong to face the current Israeli provocations," he added.
Earlier this month, Israel defied the world and angered Arabs by breaking ground on the 6,500-house settlement at the site known as Jabal Abu Ghneim in Arabic and Har Homa in Hebrew.
The project has thrown Israeli-Palestinian talks into crisis and set off 11 days of violence in the West Bank. A Palestinian suicide bomber killed three people in Tel Aviv.

Palestinian President Yasser Arafat flew to Cairo for crisis talks with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak while the PLO's political affairs chief, Farouk Kaddoumi, called on all states to cut ties with Israel for abandoning the peace process.
"The Israeli government has turned its back on the peace process and (Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu has totally destroyed this process," Kaddoumi said in Cairo.

"We demand that all (Israeli) offices be shut, all international ties suspended, all political activities halted and we demand that particularly from Europe and the United States as sponsors of the peace process," he added.

Syria, whose peace talks with Israel on the future of the Golan Heights captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war were suspended last year, has always lobbied Arabs to stop normalising ties with the Jewish state.

Syria's ally Lebanon, where Israeli forces occupy a 15 km (nine mile) deep zone in the south, said Arabs must "unify their ranks" on normalisation. Foreign Minister Faris Bouez told reporters the Arab League should adopt the "sound resolutions made by the Jerusalem Committee which met in Rabat".
Egypt and Jordan have signed peace treaties with Israel and could not easily go back on steps towards normal relations.
But Mubarak has consistently said that while official Egypt could not cut relations with the Jewish state, Egyptians could certainly boycott it unless it changed its policies.
"We have a peace treaty with Israel so you cannot tell me to stop normalisation," he told Israel's Channel Two in an interview broadcast on Saturday.
"But all that's happening affects the people, the businessmen and I bet you that businessmen who wanted to deal with you are scared to do so because you don't implement the peace treaties," he added.

Last week Oman said it had frozen ties with Israel over the settlements policy and Qatar, which froze ties with Israel in December, said on Sunday it would cease all normalisation if the Arab League decreed it.

Qatar and Oman have raced ahead of other Gulf Arab states to set up economic relations with Israel since the Jewish state signed a peace deal with the Palestinians in 1993. But they stopped short of opening diplomatic relations.
